doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Team players in a band and long-lived groups
summary: Tolliver explains choosing band members who are team players and how a few groups staying together for years propelled the art form.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You had mentioned over the years if you had a person in your band, I think the way you put it was they were engaging in something they needed to do what they were doing somewhere else. And it seems certain eras of jazz that —
You said that. It was a nice way to put it. If you’re going to do that do it with someone else.

Well I might have been referring to how I have observed, you know, those few instances when a musician may have, by the way — not by what they say but by the way they perform when they’re playing with you that their minds and persona is not as a team player. You know. And in that case it would be better for them to do their own thing or go do it somewhere else. But generally — it really depends on the flavor and what is the aspirations of anyone that calls you for a gig or what you want to have happen, you know, on the bandstand for your own gig. And that’s by sorting it out, you know, different musicians, seeing how they work and perform with you and — the good thing is that there are good choices. You don’t have to be locked down with just one set of guys. And that’s always been the case, mostly, excepting in the case when, you know, some iconic situations develop with a certain group of men, which is how this art form basically propels itself. You know we had about four or five major groups that was comprised of the same individuals for a number of years. And they helped to, you know, propel the art form forward by what they did together you know. And I think it’s a great example of, you know, the word “repertorial” of one group of players playing a set repertoire over or a style of repertoire over a number of years you know. That’s really repertory.
